title: Starting-temperature matching gave no clear day-30 cooling change in 257 Atlantic storm-buoy encounters in 1982-2024
abstract: We tested whether starting water temperature can explain late cooling after Atlantic storms in a published buoy record. We rebuilt same-date controls and required three control years within 0.5 degrees C of the starting anomaly. The common sample has 257 encounters, 134 storms and 46 buoys in 1982-2024. Matching reduced the mean starting-anomaly gap from 0.126 to 0.020 degrees C. Day-30 excess temperature changed from -0.157 to -0.098 degrees C. The paired change was +0.059 degrees C, with a conditional 95% storm-year interval of -0.025 to +0.149. Thus matching gave no clear change. The matched cooling interval also included zero; this does not show full recovery. Excluded events had stronger late cooling and larger starting gaps, so sample loss limits extension to all storms. A secondary shelf-minus-Gulf contrast stayed negative. The test reuses published observations and holds control means fixed. Source errors, reused controls and storm-linked weather limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, exact source hashes and a retrieval script are included; source records and record-level outputs stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Starting-temperature balance, mean cooling and planned matching checks. Bars show pointwise conditional 95% storm-year intervals. The primary comparison uses the same 257 encounters. Other samples differ. Control means stay fixed.

citations.reason: We reuse verified daily anomalies and encounter tables and test a different control design. This is a same-data starting-temperature balance test, not independent sensor evidence.
